emotional_catch: A mother who lost both her sons 20 years ago still waits every day with flower garlands, believing 'Mere Karan Arjun aayenge' — and the two young men who remember nothing of their past life are pulled back to her village to finish the revenge.
film_evidence: Dialogue in the clip names Karan, Arjun, Durjan Singh, Thakur and Saxena (v1 tiny transcript: 'karan Arjun' at ~288-303s, 'Durjan' at ~497s, 'Thakur', 'Saxena'); plot beats match exactly: a mother waiting with garlands for her murdered sons, two reborn young men, a palace villain, illegal arms crates at a night camp, a letter, a B&W flashback of the murder. Cross-checked against the film's known story (Wikipedia/plot summaries).

PA.evidence: Ajay = Karan reborn (Salman Khan); leaner face, long dark hair, mustache — film story + face match. Dialogue speaks "Karan" (small transcript 97-105s, 204-207s).
PA.name: Ajay (Karan)
PA.visual: Young man, leaner face, long dark hair, mustache; green / mustard shirts, jeans. NOTE: a similar-looking henchman (PT) wears mustard too — tell them apart by face (Ajay is leaner) and by story (Ajay is with Vijay / gets dragged; PT drives the jeep).

PB.evidence: Vijay = Arjun reborn (Shah Rukh Khan); curly hair, patterned vest — film story + face match. Dialogue speaks "Arjun" (small transcript 97-105s).
PB.name: Vijay (Arjun)
PB.visual: Young man, curly dark hair, patterned vest / black shirt

PC.evidence: Likely Suraj Singh (Aasif Sheikh), Durjan's son and Sonia's fiance — film story (script: "I am Durjan Singh's son and Sonia's fiancee. My name is Suraj Singh."). Purple-shirt man is prominent (tent, jeep, fight, dragging). NOT confirmed from the clip's dialogue; script calls him only "Durjan ka aadmi" (safe either way).
PC.role: villain's man — likely Suraj Singh (Durjan's son), unconfirmed
PC.visual: Purple shirt, long grey-streaked hair, mustache, cruel laugh

PD.evidence: Thakur Durjan Singh (Amrish Puri), villain; palace, riding jacket — film story + visuals. Dialogue speaks "Durjan" (small transcript 60.1s).
PD.name: Thakur Durjan Singh
PD.visual: Older heavyset man, mustache, riding jacket and boots, riding crop

PE.evidence: Munshiji = Badal Munshi (Ashok Saraf), servant of Thakur Sangram Singh — Wikipedia cast + plot. Dialogue speaks "Munshi" (small transcript 54.9-56.7s; v1 tiny).
PE.name: Munshiji
PE.visual: Yellow turban, round glasses, tilak, beige vest over white kurta; nervous, comic

PF.evidence: Seated on the veranda receiving the elder's plea (S048); talks with the elder (S045, S046). No name known — narrate as 'ghar ka malik' / 'ek aadmi'.
PF.visual: Middle-aged man, mustache, patterned kurta with a shawl

PG.evidence: Durga Singh (Raakhee), mother; white sari, garlands — film story + visuals. Dialogue speaks "Durga" (small transcript 105-109s).
PG.name: Durga
PG.visual: Older woman, white sari with head covered; grey-pink sari when holding garlands in the field

PH.evidence: Sonia Saxena (Kajol), Vijay's love; writes letters, red sari, with Durga — film story + visuals. Name not yet heard in the clip's dialogue.
PH.name: Sonia Saxena
PH.visual: Young woman, long dark hair, red and orange outfit

PI.evidence: Bindiya (Mamta Kulkarni), tomboy, Ajay's love; blue sari + mirror-work dupatta, with Durga at the end — film story + visuals. Name not yet heard in the clip's dialogue.
PI.name: Bindiya
PI.visual: Young woman, blue sari, braid, colourful mirror-work dupatta, heavy jewellery

PJ.evidence: Seated beside PF on the veranda (S048). Narrate as 'ghar ki malik' / 'ek mahila'.
PJ.visual: Middle-aged woman, green sari, gold jewellery

PK.evidence: Seated beside Durjan on the palace lawn (S002, S003). No name known — narrate as 'ek mahila'.
PK.role: woman at the palace (possibly Durjan's wife)
PK.visual: Bright pink sari and headscarf, gold jewellery; distressed

PL.evidence: Aims a pistol (S135); aims a scoped rifle (v1 S115). Narrate as 'Durjan ka aadmi'.
PL.visual: Slicked-back dark hair, thick mustache, gold earring; pistol and scoped rifle

PM.evidence: Saxena = Govind Saxena (Ranjeet), Sonia's father and Durjan's partner in the illegal arms trade — Wikipedia + plot summaries. Dialogue "Arre Saxena" (v1 tiny 30.1s).
PM.name: Mr. Saxena
PM.role: Sonia's father; Durjan's partner in the arms trade
PM.visual: Older man, greying hair, dark/light suit and tie

PN.evidence: By the jeeps facing the crowd (S009). Decide from transcript context; otherwise call him 'ek aadmi'.
PN.role: beret man — police or Durjan's man (unresolved)
PN.visual: Dark green beret, khaki jacket over black turtleneck, mustache

PO.evidence: Talks with Durjan and the elder (S217, S218, S220, S221). Minor; call him 'ek aadmi' unless the transcript names him.

PP.evidence: Sits with the elder (S227); house scenes. Narrate as 'ek aadmi'.

PQ.evidence: Beaten and left bleeding (S100-S109); cradled by a woman (S132). Per the genre rule, a random person is 'ek ladka'.
PQ.visual: Young shirtless boy in a white dhoti, beaten and bleeding

PR.evidence: Crowd scenes. Narrate as 'ek buzurg aadmi'.
PR.visual: Very old man, large white turban, white mustache and beard

PT.evidence: Drives the jeep that drags the brothers (S167, S169, S171, S173) while Ajay is the one being dragged — so he cannot be Ajay. Rounder face and thicker mustache than Ajay; always with PC/PL in villain scenes (tent S103/S105/S106). Role: Durjan's henchman (possibly Nahar or Shamsher).
PT.visual: Mustard/tan shirt and vest, rounder face, thick mustache, long dark hair

rules: Narration uses the real names from this bible only where confidence is medium or higher AND the transcript confirms the name is spoken in the clip.
Anyone with confidence low / role-only is narrated by role ('Durjan ka aadmi', 'ghar ka malik', 'ek aadmi', 'ek mahila', 'ek ladka') — never by clothes.
PA and PB are tracked by face/hair across outfit changes, never by shirt colour.
film_verification: Karan Arjun (1995), Rakesh Roshan — confirmed by dialogue (Karan, Arjun, Durga, Durjan, Munshi spoken) + web cross-check (Wikipedia, plot summaries, film script at stockq.org). No character named Rana exists in the film; the transcripts' "Rana" is a Whisper mishearing (likely Nahar, a brother-in-law).
